mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 8.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings declines, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand weakness that typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO below 96.0) intensifies supply chain constraints, increasing input costs and reducing corporate margins, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 96.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating year-over-year CPI inflation above 3.0% signals persistent price pressures that trigger hawkish monetary policy expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls above 132,000 thousand supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 132,000 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Strong residential construction activity (HOUST above 700 thousand units) fuels economic growth and corporate revenue, typically producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 700 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Declining real consumer spending (RSAFS below 400,000 million dollars) signals weakening demand that precedes revenue slowdowns, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS is below 400,000 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
